name: Projection-Rank Termination Methods and Their Universal Move
description: Packages four licensed confession routes sharing one DP rank and forgetting witness. All routes converge to one core and the fifth usable-rules route closes with explicit transport.

program.name: Certificates and Confession
program.summary: A construction method adds comparison data and verifies the original relation; a confession method transforms the problem, omits a coordinate and transports the result through a soundness theorem. The confession routes for the kernel share the canonical dependency-pair rank, the typed external-license schemas are related by quasi-functors with one irreversible license stage, and licensed transactions compose with ledgers while no rule recovers the composite semantic profile from the factor capabilities alone.

oneLine: Four distinctly licensed confession methods share one dependency-pair rank and converge to one core whose universal move carries a fifth usable-rules route closed by explicit transport.
summary: Objects are projection ranks on the KO7 schema, four licensed confession methods, their route evidence, and generic confession moves. Questions are whether distinct termination routes agree, whether they orient the duplicating step while forgetting wrapper payload, and how they project to a universal surface. All four methods share the dependency-pair rank and each orients the duplicating step while violating wrapper sensitivity. Their route evidences coincide on one common evidence object and one forgetting rank, with uniqueness under semantic-profile plus collapse hypotheses. Each family member yields a certified forgetting witness and its universal wrapper refines and is H-equivalent to the canonical DP move with minimal zero-bit discard. A fifth usable-rules route is closed with an explicit dependency-pair-to-source transport, and future routes are admitted with four rank and sigma equalities.
boundary: On the licensed transformed-call side every method orients the duplicating step downward and all four share one rank and one common route evidence. On the direct side no method is strictly sensitive to wrapper payload in either position, and rank agreement alone does not supply dependency-pair-to-source transport. The obstruction is the missing transport, recorded as open diagnostics for narrower attempts and discharged by the independent polynomial bridge that closes the fifth route; future admission is governed by the four equalities.

conclusions.statement: For every C in allConfessionMethods, C.rank equals dpConfession.rank.
The moves of the four declared universal instances are each H-equivalent to the canonical move.
The closed concrete candidate move is unconditionally H-equivalent to the canonical move.
UsableRulesS5FullClosure holds unconditionally with the concrete candidate, bridge witness, universal admission, closed fifth route and witnessed bridge-attempt equality.
For every C in allConfessionMethods and all b, s and n, C.rank (app s (recΔ b s n)) is less than C.rank (recΔ b s (delta n)).
For every C in the family, its rank fails strict wrapper sensitivity in each payload position.
For every route r, confessionRouteRank r equals dpProjection.
All four concrete route-evidence packages equal confessionGenericRouteEvidence through the generic adapter layer.
The four route evidences stored in confessionRouteConvergencePackage each equal its commonRouteEvidence.
For any rank satisfying the four semantic-profile hypotheses plus the three collapse hypotheses, that rank equals dpProjection.
For every C in the family there is a CertifiedForgettingWitness with the same rank.
If method is in allConfessionMethods then its wrapper refines the canonical DP move via family rank agreement.
If method is in allConfessionMethods then its wrapper has the canonical universal-factorization package with the stated quotient map.
If method is in allConfessionMethods then the canonical zero-bit floor is at most the method wrapper floor.
For any R, Nonempty admission holds if and only if RequirementsMet holds.

openPoints: License tags name intended routes without supplying a general termination theorem or dependency-pair-to-source transport.
Source-system termination needs an external transport theorem; rank agreement alone does not supply it.
Without an inhabited residual there is no convergence extension and no bridge.
Admission to the universal surface needs explicit equality with the canonical DP rank.
Uniqueness on full Trace needs collapse of integrate, merge and eqW; free-fragment recovery needs semantic-profile hypotheses.
Generic factorization and minimality are available with explicit characterization data; canonical profiles carry zero canonical bits.

files.summary: Defines doubled carry and confession cost curves, the CarryExceedsConfess predicate, the least crossing point, derived budgets, marginal costs and continuation rules. Proves the crossing is witnessed at the license cost, bounded by it, persistent and exactly characterized, with zero payload never crossing. Proves derived budgets force confession and separates zero-value from bounded-value stopping regimes.
files.conclusion: For nonzero payload the carry and confession cost curves cross at a computable point bounded by the license price and stay crossed, with sharp zero-payload failure and explicit stopping regimes.

files.summary: Defines SoundnessLicense tags and ConfessionMethod as a ProjectionRank paired with a license. Constructs the method-agnostic confession-core witness by forgetting the tag. Proves every method orients the duplicating step and violates wrapper sensitivity in both positions.
files.conclusion: Every confession method orients the duplicating step while violating wrapper sensitivity, after forgetting its license tag.

files.summary: Defines an argument-filtering witness, counter rank function, constructorwise filter and route evidence into unary counter syntax. Proves the rank equals the registered dependency-pair projection, computes the filtered duplicating shapes and packages the projection-rank profile. The soundness license is only a route-classification tag without a source termination transfer.
files.conclusion: Argument filtering yields the same rank as the dependency-pair projection and the same filtered counter step, with only a rank-profile result.

files.summary: Defines direct and original-symbol subterm relations, a counter-coordinate witness, its rank function and route evidence. Proves the rank equals the DP projection with strict counter descent and wrapper erasure, and that the witness satisfies the generic semantic profile. The license tag names the intended route without supplying a general termination theorem.
files.conclusion: Direct counter projection yields the same rank as the dependency-pair projection with strict counter descent and wrapper erasure.

files.summary: Packages the KO7 dependency-pair route with dpProjection strictly decreasing on the recursive pair and well-founded reverse relation. Pairs dpProjectionRank with the Arts-Giesl license tag as metadata without a general processor soundness theorem. Forgets pair-specific fields to the generic route-evidence profile.
files.conclusion: The dependency-pair route packages strict pair descent and well-foundedness with the same projection rank used by the other routes.

files.summary: Collects four confession methods on the KO7 schema with shared DP rank and distinct license tags. Proves duplicating-step orientation, sensitivity violations, certified-forgetting conversion, pair-problem termination and imported polynomial termination. Records the gap with no direct whole-term witness closed by a licensed transformed-call route for every member.
files.conclusion: Four distinctly licensed methods share one rank, orient the duplicating step, supply certified forgetting, and jointly resolve payload-level operational incompleteness.

files.summary: Specifies the data and four equalities required to admit an additional confession route to the universal-instance interface. Proves admission is equivalent to meeting those requirements. Gives two conditional noncomputable example constructions for RPO-with-marks and polynomial-interpretation routes.
files.conclusion: Future confession routes are admitted exactly when the four rank and sigma equalities are met.

files.summary: The file defines supporting-module tags, hypothesis vocabulary, a boundary-entry record and a lookup assigning each of six universal-confession theorem identifiers a recorded status. All six entries are recorded as theorem-projected with no required hypothesis, one carrying an L2 tag. It defines four ledger buckets and a witness predicate linking statuses to buckets, with three conditional buckets empty. It proves the lookup status equals the ledger status, each entry satisfies its bucket witness, and each theorem identifier has a unique witnessing status.
files.conclusion: The ledger records all six universal-confession theorems as theorem-projected with empty conditional buckets.

files.summary: Packages the four concrete confession routes and their generic adapters into one convergence package with a common route-evidence object and forgetting witness. Proves the four routes agree, recover the DP rank, and satisfy rank corollaries. Defines the usable-rules residual obligation that additionally demands an explicit dependency-pair-to-source transport.
files.conclusion: All four confession routes collapse to one shared route-evidence object with DP rank, while a usable-rules route needs extra explicit transport.

files.summary: Builds the size-change termination route for the step-duplicating schema as a single call graph with strict counter descent and non-increasing other arguments. Defines the SCT witness, counter rank function and derived projection rank, and proves equality with the dependency-pair rank. Packages the result as an SCT confession and route evidence satisfying the generic semantic profile.
files.conclusion: The SCT route yields the same counter-depth rank as dependency pairs and locally orients the duplicating step.

files.summary: Isolates the convergence layer for dependency-pair, counter-projection, size-change and argument-filtering routes. Defines the shared DP-based confession core and extended collapse conditions, proves a uniqueness theorem and that all local witnesses, projection ranks, generic route evidences and forgetting witnesses coincide. Factors the core through the free shadow and summarizes convergence.
files.conclusion: The four distinct routes converge to one shared confession core, rank and forgetting-witness layer.

files.summary: The file re-exports route and theorem identifiers, statuses, boundary entries and future-route admission as API aliases. It defines count functions from ledger lists for routes, theorem statuses, bridge-attempt results and tagged entries, plus two aggregate count structures. It proves the recorded counts equal 5 theorem-backed routes, 6 theorem-projected theorems, 2 bridge-attempt results, 1 tagged entry and 0 in each conditional and blocked bucket, each holding by definition of the explicit lists.
files.conclusion: The API records five theorem-backed routes, six theorem-projected theorems, two bridge-attempt results and empty conditional and blocked buckets.

files.summary: Packages confession methods and route evidence as generic confession moves under explicit equality with the canonical DP rank. Defines the canonical move and abstract information profiles with zero canonical bits. Proves mutual identity refinements and H-equivalences, builds characterization, optimality and minimality data, and assembles the four named universal instances plus a future-instance projection.
files.conclusion: All four method wrappers are H-equivalent to the canonical DP move via identity refinements.

files.summary: The file defines route identifiers, statuses and a five-entry route ledger all recorded as theorem-backed, plus a two-entry discharged bridge-obligation ledger. It defines a lookup giving each theorem-backed route a concrete universal move and proves each has such a move and is H-equivalent to the canonical confession move, the usable-rules case unconditionally. It defines theorem identifiers, statuses and a six-entry theorem ledger all recorded as theorem-projected with empty conditional lists. It proves the ledger lengths and the closed usable-rules status by definition.
files.conclusion: Every listed theorem-backed route is recorded with a universal move H-equivalent to the canonical confession move, with all five routes and six theorems recorded as theorem-backed and theorem-projected and no conditional or blocked entries.

files.summary: Packages admitted usable-rules residuals and the concrete candidate into the universal confession surface. Proves identity refinements and H-equivalences to the canonical move and supplies characterization, optimality and minimality data. Exports a closed canonical usable-rules instance using the independently inhabited soundness bridge.
files.conclusion: Every admitted usable-rules residual, including the closed concrete candidate, is H-equivalent to the canonical confession move.

files.summary: Defines the conditional usable-rules convergence wrapper built from an inhabited residual obligation. Proves any residual projects to the common core, common route evidence and DP forgetting rank while exposing its explicit transport. Establishes equivalence between residual existence and wrapper inhabitation, and emptiness of the wrapper without a residual.
files.conclusion: Usable-rules convergence data exist exactly when an explicit proof-bearing residual exists.

files.summary: Retains obstruction diagnostics for two narrower usable-rules construction routes that supply rank agreement but no DP-to-source transport. Records the canonical bridge inhabited by the independent KO7 termination theorem with both labelled attempts witnessed. Proves admission equivalent to bridge inhabitation and the fifth route closed.
files.conclusion: The canonical bridge witnesses the usable-rules transport, closing the fifth route with both labelled attempts witnessed.

files.summary: Defines the concrete usable-rules candidate from the shared core and route evidence and the bridge type demanding DP-to-source transport. Discharges the bridge via the independent full-system polynomial termination theorem without inferring generic processor soundness. Builds the canonical residual and proves the route inhabited with the boundary closed.
files.conclusion: The canonical usable-rules candidate is unconditionally inhabited via the independent polynomial termination bridge.

files.summary: This file records the closed five-row usable-rules surface. It defines status kinds, row identifiers, rows and a catalog structure bundling the candidate, bridge, universal admission, historical diagnostic and bridge-attempt result. It proves the catalog contains all five rows with their expected kinds and that its projections recover the candidate, route agreement, forgetting rank, residual package and witnesses. It closes with an unconditional conjunction stating the fifth confession route is fully inhabited.
files.conclusion: The fifth confession route is unconditionally closed with all five usable-rules rows inhabited.

files.summary: The file defines an abstract confession-move interface with quotient, projection, residual obstruction and verifier fields, all results conditional on an inhabitant. It defines refinement witnesses and mutual refinement with reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. It proves certificates imply residuals, residuals imply verdicts, and refinements transport verdicts across projections.
files.conclusion: Refinement is reflexive and transitive and mutual refinement is an equivalence preserving verdicts across projections.

files.summary: This file gives proof-bearing interfaces for information profiles, universal factorization and optimality for confession moves. It wraps KO7 confession-method ranks as generic moves, builds universal, optimality and discarded-information packages from rank agreement, and proves generic and KO7-specific factorization, convergence-as-H-equivalence, universal-property and discarded-bit minimality theorems.
files.conclusion: Every theorem-backed KO7 confession method factors through the canonical DP move with the canonical discarded-bit floor.

files.summary: This file builds a four-route confession index with concrete evidence for dependency pairs, direct counter projection, size-change termination and argument filtering, and reads each retained rank from that evidence. It proves all four ranks equal the same counter projection and induce the same full term order, so the confession full-order quotient has exactly one class while route origins and licenses stay distinct. It also builds an infinite base-sensitive family of actual KO7 dependency-pair reduction pairs with pairwise distinct full orders, so the quotient of all such pairs is infinite, as is the construction-side root-orienter quotient. The culminating package contrasts infinitely many construction classes with one confession class and no injective map between them.
files.conclusion: The file proves the exact moduli package of infinitely many construction classes, one confession class for the four canonical routes with distinct origins and licenses, infinitely many actual dependency-pair classes, and no injective construction-to-confession quotient map.

files.summary: This file defines weak cost crossing and cost ties for doubled carry and confession burdens, a three-way burden order with an executable comparison, least weak crossing depths with bounded executable weak and strict searches, a cubic cumulative carry sum, and optimal action sets with tie-break policies. It proves that positive payload yields a weak crossing, that ties occur at most at a single depth, that zero payload admits a tie in a single degenerate case and never reaches strict crossing, and that executable searches return the mathematical least thresholds. It orders the weak threshold below the strict threshold, showing the strict threshold equals the weak threshold or its successor according to whether the weak threshold is strict or a tie. It also proves a closed cubic identity for cumulative carry burden and reuses finite-horizon stopping characterizations, including a fixture showing zero immediate gain alone does not imply stopping.
files.conclusion: With positive payload the executable weak and strict searches return the least mathematical thresholds with the strict threshold equal to the weak threshold or its successor depending on tie status.

files.summary: This module distinguishes two workload conventions for carry costs, namely charging each depth once versus recomputing every prefix. It proves the once-through sum equals the existing quadratic direct burden and the every-prefix sum equals the existing cubic cumulative burden, with exact closed forms and recurrences. It shows positive payload makes recomputation strictly more expensive and zero payload makes both zero.
files.conclusion: The file proves that cached single-execution cost is quadratic while every-prefix recomputation is cubic, with exact closed forms and strict separation for positive payload.

files.summary: This file preserves compatibility identifiers around a closed seven-constructor syntax, a constant collapse map, and a two-term noninjectivity witness. It packages scope and dependency text in a diagnostic record with a default value. It imports the mass-growth comparison to prove that recursor and circular measures satisfy MassIndistinguishable under the three displayed normalization equations.
files.conclusion: The constant map identifies distinct closed recursor terms and the recursor and circular mass profiles satisfy MassIndistinguishable under the three normalization equations.

files.summary: This file proves equality of two recursor terms under any Sigma homomorphism into an algebra whose recR ignores its third argument, with a corollary contradiction from an added distinguishing hypothesis. It proves both orbit mass functions satisfy MassIndistinguishable under the three normalization equations. It proves licensed acceptance coincides with the strong-normalization verdict and that the concrete recursor system is accepted by its transformed-call certificate.
files.conclusion: A Sigma homomorphism into a third-constant algebra identifies the two witnesses, both orbit mass profiles satisfy MassIndistinguishable, and licensed acceptance for KO7 systems holds exactly for strongly normalizing systems with the recursor system accepted.

files.summary: This file defines abstract burden and entropy numerics for canonical-trace analysis, including doubled confessed burdens, quadratic and linear normalizers, and proof-entropy size, value and overhead functions. It proves closed-form summation identities and real-limit behaviour where quadratic and linear normalizers tend to p over two and w over two, burden ratios eventually dominate any bound for positive payload, and proof entropy tends to one for positive steps as payload grows while staying monotone. The header stresses these are stipulated numeric models and that a bridge to trace-term observations needs separate declarations.
files.conclusion: Doubled burdens grow quadratically with limits p over two and w over two while proof entropy is monotone and tends to one as payload grows.

files.summary: This file defines a schema-generic forgetting witness as a rank that orients the duplicating step while explicitly violating wrapper sensitivity on both payload positions. It provides constructors from projection ranks, confession-core witnesses, semantic profiles with four hypotheses, and route evidence, each preserving the rank. It also adds a ConfessionMethod adapter that yields a forgetting witness via its projection rank, noting the package records counterexamples and orientation without claiming causation.
files.conclusion: Every projection, confession-core, semantic, route and confession-method rank yields a forgetting witness with the same rank.

files.summary: This file is a reach gate for the confession crossing point. It checks cost functions, the carry-exceeds-confess predicate, decidability, existence and leastness of the crossing point, and marginal and stopping-regime lemmas with axiom queries. It adds computed witnesses showing the crossing bound, equality of doubled costs, and presence and absence of exceeding at small depths.
files.conclusion: A least crossing point exists where carry exceeds confession with concrete witnesses at small parameters.

files.summary: This file checks FutureRouteRequirements, universal admission and the iff between admission and requirements met plus two schema examples. It provides three parameterized examples that build universal admissions from rank, projection and sigma equalities. It proves no new theory and only exercises the schema surface.
files.conclusion: Under matching rank, projection and sigma hypotheses the RPO-with-marks and polynomial-interpretation schemas admit a universal surface.

files.summary: This file checks the confession-method optimality-boundary ledger. It verifies statuses, required hypotheses, and supporting-phase modules for universal theorems, including file labels and the unique-status exhaustiveness witness for gauge-fixing identity.
files.conclusion: The optimality-boundary ledger marks the checked universal theorems as theorem-projected with stated hypotheses and phase modules and is exhaustive for gauge-fixing identity.

files.summary: This file checks the universal API counts and ledger entries for confession-method routes and theorems. It verifies exact counts for theorem-backed, conditional, blocked, projected, optimality, information, cost, bridge-attempt, and tagged categories, plus status-count record projections and confession-cost-floor ledger fields.
files.conclusion: The universal API counts are exact as stated, with five theorem-backed routes, six theorem-projected theorems, two bridge attempts, and matching status records.

files.summary: This file checks verdicts, generic and information-theoretic moves, rank equalities, refinement and equivalence lemmas, and four universal instances. It includes controls deriving refinement, HEquivalence and discarded-bits minimality for DP, counter-projection, SCT and argument-filtering. It also checks the joint equivalence of all routes and a future SCT projection.
files.conclusion: All four universal instances are HEquivalent to the canonical move with minimal discarded information.

files.summary: This file checks universal route and theorem ledgers, bridge obligations, their lengths and statuses, and projection lemmas. It includes controls that the usableRules route is theorem-backed with discharged obligations and canonical HEquivalence. It fixes ledger lengths at five routes and six theorems with no conditional or blocked entries.
files.conclusion: The ledger holds five theorem-backed routes and six projected theorems with usableRules closed and canonically equivalent.

files.summary: This file checks residual rank, canonical route moves, refinement and HEquivalence, and universal characterization data for the usable-rules residual. It provides five parameterized controls over a soundness bridge deriving rank equality, characterization, refinement, equivalence and minimality. It proves no new theory beyond exercising the bridge-conditional surface.
files.conclusion: Under a soundness bridge the usable-rules residual has correct rank, refines canonical and minimizes discarded bits.

files.summary: This file checks concrete bridge witnesses, universal admission, local witness fields, common route moves, soundness obstructions and attempt results including Arts-Giesl and LCEL variants. It includes controls fixing obstruction fields, witnessed outcomes and the iff between admission and bridge-witnessed. It closes with the fifth usable-rules route.
files.conclusion: All bridge attempts are witnessed and universal admission is inhabited exactly when a bridge witness exists.

files.summary: This file checks the five-row usable-rules final-status catalog and its projections. It verifies row coverage and availability marks for candidate, wrapper, diagnostic, bridge, and fifth route, and that the catalog projects the concrete candidate, route agreement, forgetting rank, residual package, universal wrapper and admission, bridge witness, and S5 closure.
files.conclusion: The five-row final-status catalog holds with the stated availability marks and projections to candidate, rank, residual, wrapper, admission, bridge, and S5 closure.

files.summary: This file checks usable-rules residual, candidate, and bridge obligations for the confession route. It verifies local witness inhabitation, substrate evidence, projections to common route evidence and forgetting rank, explicit soundness-bridge requirements, convergence-extension equivalences, and conditions under which missing bridges block the route.
files.conclusion: Usable-rules convergence requires an explicit residual and soundness bridge, with the concrete candidate satisfying agreement and rank projections and blocking otherwise.

files.summary: This file is a paired reach and trust-surface gate for construction and confession moduli. It checks confession routes, evidence, ranks, licenses, full-order equivalence and quotients, and base-sensitive DP ranks with infinitude. It proves no new content and only audits reachability and axioms.
files.conclusion: The confession quotient is a singleton while the DP full-order quotient is infinite with exact moduli.

files.summary: This file inventories the public surface for cost comparison including weak crossing, ties, burden order, compareBurden, crossing points, cumulative costs, ratios, optimal actions and stopping regions. It pairs each declaration with an axiom query including generated projections and constructors. It proves no new content and only records the current source surface.
files.conclusion: Burden comparison has decidable weak and tie structure with least crossing points and stopping behavior.

files.summary: This file is a paired reach and axiom inventory for CostWorkloadSemantics. It checks direct, cached-trace and repeated-prefix doubled costs with equalities to direct and cumulative costs. It also checks closedness, successor, growth comparison, zero-payload workloads and the growth pair.
files.conclusion: Cached and repeated-prefix costs match direct and cumulative forms with strict growth for positive payloads.

files.summary: This file defines a toy verdict on naturals that holds exactly at zero and a toy GenericConfessionMove instance over Nat with unit license, identity projection and verdict-indexed residual and verifier. It checks the public surface of the confession-move framework, including refinement, transport and equivalence lemmas. Six examples prove the residual, barrier and verdict at zero and the reflexive refinement and heterogeneous equivalence of the toy move.
files.conclusion: The toy move is a valid confession-move instance whose barrier, residual and verdict all hold exactly at zero with reflexive refinement and equivalence.

files.summary: This file is a reachability and axiom audit for the Recursor DPConfessionLicense module. It resolves the recursor term, the void collapse of dependency pairs, and the partial-progress claim. It prints axiom dependencies for the statements that dependency-pair projection fails substitution invariance, lies outside the recursor signature, and governs termination and soundness through an external observer license.
files.conclusion: The file records that the recursor dependency-pair license definitions and external-observer termination statements resolve and reports their axiom dependencies.

files.summary: This file exercises the usable-rules soundness-bridge attempt and its universal admission counterpart. It checks the concrete substrate evidence, bridge witness and universal admission against their axiom dependencies. It checks that the obstruction lists source soundness transport as open, that the recorded attempt value is witnessed, and that universal admission and bridge-witness inhabitation correspond.
files.conclusion: The file checks that concrete universal admission is inhabited if and only if a concrete bridge witness is inhabited, with the attempt recorded as witnessed and the fifth confession route closed while source soundness transport remains listed as open.
